learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Chose About 4 and locked it in, against About 1.6 and Fewer than 1.
observations.exploration: Initial 0%: 40 infected contacts from ten cases, R 4.0. Clicked 60%: 24 of 40 contacts immune, 16 infected, R 1.6. Clicked 75%: 30 immune, ten infected, R 1.0. Attempted slider setValue 100 was rejected by browser input API and state stayed 75%; no lesson defect inferred.
observations.reveal: Show me why corrected prediction to About 1.6, connected 16 infections/10 cases to 4 × 0.4, stated smooth reduction before threshold and random mixing, perfect immunity, made-up disease limits.
observations.visual: Actual inline screenshot inspected at 1257 × 936 dark viewport. Dot town and contact lines visibly distinguish immune, susceptible, case and infected states. Lower reveal extends below viewport; visible DOM provided full text.
observations.blinding: 4/4 claims checked chrome visible and ignored.

prediction.reason: Numerical alternatives distinguish no benefit from subthreshold reduction.

interaction.reason: Changing immune share visibly changes contacts and R.

payoff.reason: Connects observed contact counts to formula and explicitly limits toy model.

clarity.reason: Two preset controls and numerical feedback make tested sequence understandable.

transfer.reason: Reusable susceptible-share relation and conditions stated, but no new application.
transfer.evidence: R0 × susceptible share and toy-model caveat.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast, phone, zoom and motion untested.

surprise.reason: No-benefit prediction is contradicted before threshold.

visualExplanation.reason: Contact colors carry cancellation of infection opportunities.
visualExplanation.evidence: Dot town screenshot and contact totals.

playfulness.reason: Presets allow reversible comparison; slider not successfully exercised.

practicalValue.reason: Provides concrete interpretation of subthreshold immunity in the stated toy setting.
practicalValue.evidence: Reveal distinguishes reduction from R threshold.

depth.reason: Smooth reduction and threshold differ meaningfully, with model limits stated.

complexity.reason: Connects proportions to average infections and threshold.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Two linked relations: susceptible share determines mean infection count; mean relative to one determines growth threshold.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low on tested desktop; reveal bottom requires more vertical space.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: moderate: R and herd threshold introduced.

whyCool: Changing immunity from 60% to 75% visibly removes six more infections while R falls from 1.6 to one.
caveat: Only preset states tested; the reveal calls 75% both R=1 and the point where R drops below one, a small boundary wording ambiguity.
missingEvidence: Slider endpoint attempt rejected by browser API; full boundary not tested.
Keyboard, focus, contrast, phone, zoom/reflow and motion checks not performed.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
